html:
SMTO-CTR-0014 — SMTO rejected a task plan that went beyond your request

GUID: 29afd0b0-a297-443e-8298-9dc6316d80e9
Slug: task-contract-scope-broadened
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • The plan SMTO wrote for your request used files, folders or saved @ values you didn't give, or would change things you said to only look at. SMTO didn't act on this plan.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Task contract step under the task and read the Task Contract Integrity Guard section. It lists the file path or @ reference the check objected to. That item is exactly what the plan added or changed without your request backing it.
  2. If that file, folder or @ value is what you meant, write it into your request exactly. If you used an @ reference, make sure the plan should keep it unchanged. The guard only accepts locations and saved values that appear in your own words.
  3. If you asked SMTO to only look or read, keep that wording, and don't ask it to change things in the same request. A plan that changes things is rejected when your request says to only read.
  4. Send the corrected request as a new message. Retry on the old task reuses your original wording, so use it only if your request didn't need changes. Your request now names what to use, so it's safe to try again; a fresh plan is checked from scratch.

What success looks like

  • The Task contract step shows Task contract generated and the task starts working.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with your request text, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't switch off Task Contract Integrity Guard to get the task through; it is what stopped the plan from touching things you didn't name.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Task Contract was rejected for broadened authority: the enabled Integrity Guard found an unprovenanced or traversing scope path, or an invented or dropped @parameter reference, or the offline scope check found mutation/mixed scope against a read-only source.

What this means

  • The enabled integrity gate rejects authority provenance, or an offline scope diagnostic detects mutation/mixed scope against an explicit read-only source. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • The enabled integrity gate rejects authority provenance, or an offline scope diagnostic detects mutation/mixed scope against an explicit read-only source.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect integrity findings and whether the check was the live provenance gate or the separate offline scope diagnostic.

How to fix it

  • Open the failed attempt in the Task contract activity and read the 'Task Contract Integrity Guard' findings (unprovenanced_scope_path, scope_path_traversal, invented_parameter_reference, parameter_reference_not_preserved) or the offline scope_broadened reason from validate_contract. Make intended paths and @parameter references explicit in the source (or align read-only wording with the intent), then use Retry or resubmit; integrity failures are never auto-retried, and turning off task_contract_integrity_guard_enabled is not the routine fix. Earlier revisions' effects stay governed by their own receipts.
  • Correct the recorded authority violation through the existing compilation flow while keeping the integrity guard enabled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported flow preserves source authority and any enabled integrity gate passes.

What not to do

  • Do not disable the integrity guard as a default fix.
  • Do not disable the integrity guard as the routine fix for broadened scope.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
